cards.title: Use platform ROAS directionally within the same platform
cards.claim: ROAS and CPA can provide directional campaign and ad feedback within a platform, but cross-platform ROAS comparisons can mislead because platforms have different attribution models and funnel roles.
cards.action: Compare ROAS between campaigns within the same platform; do not use it to compare Google and Meta campaigns for larger business-level decisions.
applies_when: Reviewing campaign or ad performance inside one advertising platform
Using in-platform attributed metrics such as ROAS or CPA
do_not_use_when: Making larger business-level budget decisions from platform-attributed ROAS alone
unknowns: Which attribution settings and campaign structures make within-platform comparisons sufficiently comparable
How to combine platform metrics with financial-grade or incrementality measurement
evidence_quotes: "They are helpful in directional campaign feedback and ad feedback within the siloed platform."
"what would be a big mistake is comparing a rorowaz number on a Google campaign to a rorowaz number on a meta campaign because they have different attribution models."
"if we're looking at two meta campaigns next to each other, we can compare rorowaz, we can use that to make decisions."

cards.title: Use new-customer revenue rather than total revenue for media efficiency
cards.claim: A total revenue-to-ad-spend metric can credit paid marketing for returning-customer revenue that may have occurred without paid ads; the passage recommends using new-customer revenue divided by ad spend instead.
cards.action: Strip returning customer revenue from the calculation and use new customer revenue divided by ad spend rather than total revenue divided by ad spend.
do_not_use_when: Returning-customer revenue cannot be separated from new-customer revenue
Treating the resulting metric as proof of campaign incrementality
unknowns: The exact definition of a new customer
Whether the resulting new-customer metric is profitable for a given business
